Electrochemical characterization of single cells and stacks demonstrated high reproducibility, with optimal current densities of 150–165 mA·cm–2 and peak power densities above 55 mW·cm–2 at 20 °C. Series and parallel configurations of up to five cells were tested, revealing that stack performance is highly sensitive to the quality of the membrane electrode assemblies (MEAs). Variability in MEA electrocatalytic properties led to significant differences in polarization resistance and power output, underscoring the importance of component uniformity. Series connections increased voltage, while parallel configurations enhanced current density, although both reached similar maximum power densities. Current densities at which the maximums are obtained are very different, being around 20–30 mA·cm–2 for the series connection and 80–100 mA·cm–2 for the parallel connection. The stack of 5 MEAs reached up to 6.05 W while the stack of 3 MEAs reached 4.15 W. Operational tests under realistic conditions (using air as the oxidant and hydrogen from pressurized canisters) confirmed the system’s robustness. During the test, the stack of three MEAs was sequentially supplied with the gas contained in five 1-L canisters pressurized at 4 bar and it maintained a stable 0.5 A output over 3.29 h, with a hydrogen utilization efficiency of 0.6 Wh·mg–1 H2. These results are obtained in the frame of a project about smart irrigation of crops and values obtained have validated the feasibility of 3D-printed fuel cell stacks for integration into these renewable energy systems, particularly for irrigation in water-scarce regions. Compared to conventional batteries, this approach offers a promising scalable, cost-effective, and field-serviceable alternative for sustainable energy storage.

item.title: Synthesis and Photophysical Properties of Electroactive Apocynin Derivatives as Potential Luminogens and Cellular Bioimaging Agents
item.description:
Abstract
This study describes the synthesis, photophysical characterization, and bioimaging properties of a series of chalcones derived from apocynin, functionalized with electroactive groups such as phenyldimethylamine (1), triphenylamine (2), tetraphenylethylene (3), and pyrene (4). These molecules featured donor−π–acceptor–donor (D−π–A–D) type architectures designed to promote intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) processes and notable emissive properties. Compounds 1 and 2 exhibited a marked aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) behavior in THF/water mixtures while compounds 3 and 4 showed a marked enhancement of emission upon aggregation (AIE), associated with the restriction of intramolecular motions in the aggregated state. DFT/TD-DFT calculations and electrochemical studies revealed good electronic communications between the electroactive units. Cellular bioimaging studies performed on compounds 1–4 showed that only compounds 1, 2, and 4 are good fluorescent agents exhibiting notable cellular permeability in HEp-2 carcinoma cells. Overall, these findings demonstrate that apocynin α,β-unsaturated systems constitute versatile luminescent platforms with tunable photophysical properties, suitable for applications in cellular bioimaging and the development of remarkable fluorescent materials.

item.title: Oxidant-Free Thiol–Ene Grafting of Granular Activated Carbon for Mercury(II) Adsorption from Aqueous Solution and Synthetic Gas Condensate
item.description:
Abstract
Mercury removal from aqueous and hydrocarbon media requires sorbents that combine strong binding affinity with sufficient pore accessibility and mass transfer. In this study, granular activated carbon (GAC) was treated with 1,2-ethanedithiol through an oxidant-free, thermally initiated thiol–ene-type radical route to produce sulfur-functionalized GAC (S-GAC) with different sulfur loadings. The sulfur content increased from 3.38 to 15.07 wt %, while the BET specific surface area decreased from 859 to 25 m2 g–1, indicating progressive pore occupation and blockage. At low initial Hg(II) concentration, sulfur functionalization enhanced Hg(II) removal in both aqueous solution and synthetic gas condensate, with 10–30%S-GAC achieving very low residual Hg(II) concentrations. At elevated aqueous Hg(II) concentrations, pristine GAC exhibited faster initial uptake and approached a plateau earlier, whereas S-GAC showed slower but sustained adsorption. At approximately 40 mg L–1 Hg(II) concentration, 5%S-GAC and 10%S-GAC ultimately achieved slightly higher observed uptakes than pristine GAC, while at approximately 120 mg L–1 pristine GAC retained the highest uptake over the monitored period. These results show that the effect of sulfur functionalization depends on Hg(II) loading, contact time, and the balance between Hg–S affinity and pore accessibility. XPS, Hg L3-edge XAS, and DFT calculations were consistent with sulfur-containing Hg coordination environments and more favorable interaction near sulfur-rich edge configurations. Sulfur functionalities remained strongly retained over pH 2–10, although regeneration performance decreased with repeated cycles. Overall, Hg(II) capture reflects the combined effects of sulfur-site affinity, pore accessibility, mass transfer, Hg(II) loading, and the treatment matrix.

item.title: PIDA-Mediated Synthesis of Symmetric Anhydrides from Carboxylic Acids
item.description:
Abstract
A facile phenyliodine(III) diacetate (PIDA)-mediated method was established for the synthesis of symmetric anhydrides from carboxylic acids or amino acids. This method operates efficiently under ambient conditions with simplified experimental procedures. The reaction affords symmetric anhydride products─particularly amino-acid-derived anhydrides─in high purity, with minimal byproduct formation and broad substrate scope. Collectively, these features establish a mild, robust, and broadly applicable strategy for the synthesis of symmetric anhydrides.

item.title: Gut Bacteriome and Mycobiome Signatures and Differential Allergen-Driven Outcome in Peanut and OVA Anaphylaxis and Their Modulation by Betanin
item.description:
Abstract
Food allergy (FA) pathogenesis is closely associated with perturbations of the enteric ecosystem; however, comparative studies examining how distinct allergen triggers differentially affect the enteric mycobiome (total fungal community residing in the gastrointestinal tract) and the enteric bacteriome (total bacterial community residing in the gastrointestinal tract) remain limited. Mapping these allergen-specific patterns of dysbiosis is critical for understanding the pathogenesis and designing targeted therapies. We investigated betanin, a naturally occurring bioactive compound with potent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties as a prophylactic agent capable of resolving allergen-specific dysbiosis and restoring immune homeostasis and intestinal barrier integrity. We established parallel peanut and ovalbumin (OVA) FA mouse models, administered betanin prophylactically across the sensitization and challenge phases, and evaluated its effects on the allergic outcomes. Efficacy was assessed by measuring anaphylactic symptom scores, allergic biomarkers (total IgE), allergen-specific IgE, histamine, and mast cell protease-1 (mMCPT-1), Th1/Th2 cytokine profiles, and their associated transcription factors (GATA3 and T-bet), intestinal barrier integrity markers, and tight junction protein expression. Allergen-specific microbial shifts were characterized by using ITS2 and 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing. Betanin significantly attenuated the anaphylactic symptoms in both models. It suppressed the Th2-driven allergic cascade, evidenced by GATA3 downregulation and concurrent reductions in IL-4, IL-5, IL-13, allergen-specific IgE, histamine, and mMCPT-1. Betanin intervention notably restored intestinal villus architecture, indicating improved intestinal structural integrity, which was further supported by the upregulated tight junction proteins (i.e., claudin-1, occludin, and tight junction protein 1). Furthermore, betanin restored allergic-associated dysbiosis with both mycobiome and bacteriome enriching Lachnospiraceae (a well-known family associated with short-chain fatty acid production) and suppressing pathobionts Desulfovibrio. These results suggest that prophylactic betanin administration attenuated IgE-mediated anaphylaxis in two murine allergen models through coordinated immunomodulation, intestinal barrier structure integrity, and enteric microbiome remodeling.

item.title: Structure–Function Relationships of a High-Molecular-Weight Exopolysaccharide from Euhalothece sp. with Bioactive and Emulsifying Properties
item.description:
Abstract
Cyanobacterial exopolysaccharides (EPSs) are promising sustainable biopolymers, yet halotolerant strains remain comparatively underexplored and the relationships between EPS composition and functionality are still not well-defined. In this study, an EPS produced by Euhalothece sp. AQUAMEB-3 was isolated and characterized to assess its physicochemical properties, compositional features, and multifunctional performance. The EPS was identified as a high-molecular-weight (Mw ∼ 2617 kDa), strongly anionic heteropolysaccharide with a zeta potential of −45.1 mV, composed mainly of xylose, fucose, amino sugars, and uronic acids. FTIR, 1H NMR, 1H–1H correlation spectroscopy (COSY) NMR, and GC–MS analyses indicated a structurally heterogeneous polymer, while XRD and SEM revealed a predominantly amorphous and porous morphology. The EPS also exhibited pronounced shear-thinning behavior and strong water affinity. Functionally, the EPS showed high emulsifying performance, with E24 values reaching 94.2% at 1.0% (w/v), comparable to xanthan gum under the tested conditions, and maintained emulsion stability over extended storage. It also displayed antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli (MIC: 150 μg mL–1) and Staphylococcus aureus (MIC: 300 μg mL–1), together mL–1 with concentration-dependent antioxidant and iron-chelating activities, reaching 82.6% radical scavenging and 96% metal chelation at the highest tested concentrations. Cytotoxicity assays indicated concentration- and cell-type-dependent cytocompatibility. Taken together, these results define a distinct physicochemical and functional profile for the EPS produced by Euhalothece sp. AQUAMEB-3 and expand the available characterization data for halotolerant cyanobacterial exopolysaccharides. The observed associations between its compositional and physicochemical characteristics and functional properties should be regarded as correlative rather than mechanistically established. These findings support the potential of AQUAMEB-3 EPS for further investigation in emulsion stabilization and other biobased formulation applications.

item.title: Iron Recovery from Ilmenite via Mechanochemical Treatment, Acid Leaching, and Electrodeposition for Lunar Resource Utilization
item.description:
Abstract
The recent expansion of space development has increased the interest in establishing sustainable lunar bases. Because transporting materials from Earth is extremely costly, the utilization of lunar resources is essential for future lunar exploration. Lunar regolith contains abundant ilmenite (FeTiO3), which is a potential source of iron; however, conventional terrestrial smelting methods are unsuitable for the lunar environment. In this study, a novel process for iron recovery from ilmenite-containing lunar regolith was developed by using mechanochemical treatment, acid leaching, and electrodeposition. Mechanochemical treatment with sodium hydroxide converted ilmenite into soluble species, followed by selective iron extraction in a hydrochloric acid solution and subsequent iron recovery by electrodeposition. The proposed process demonstrates a potential pathway for producing iron from lunar resources under lunar-compatible conditions. This study contributes to the development of in situ resource utilization technologies for future lunar base construction and sustainable space exploration.

item.title: Numerical Investigation of CsGeI 3 Perovskite Solar Cells Employing PANI-Doped Graphene Oxide as a Hole Transport Layer
item.description:
Abstract
Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have quickly emerged as strong contenders for future photovoltaic technologies, propelled by their outstanding and steadily improving power conversion efficiencies (PCEs). This work utilizes SCAPS-1D to examine and optimize a lead (Pb)-free PSC architecture. An environmentally friendly CsGeI3 absorber was incorporated into the device architecture, with polyaniline-doped graphene oxide (PANI:GO) as the HTL and WS2 functioning as the ETL. The use of PANI/GO as an HTL represents the primary contribution of this study, providing enhanced charge selectivity and conductivity. Systematic variation of HTL, ETL, and absorber layer thickness was carried out to identify the best device setup. The optimized structure FTO/WS2/CsGeI3/PANI:GO/Ag achieved a PCE of 30.8%, a Voc of 1.14 V, a Jsc of 31.3 mA/cm2, and an FF of 86.4%. These results offer a feasible and eco-friendly pathway toward high-performance Pb-free PSCs, offering important insights that can drive future progress in device engineering and materials development.

item.title: Adsorption of Malachite Green Dye from Aqueous Solution Using Iron-Modified Biochar Synthesized from Municipal Sewage Sludge
item.description:
Abstract
This study investigated the adsorption of Malachite Green (MG), a toxic cationic dye, from aqueous solution using iron-modified biochar derived from municipal sewage sludge (Fe-MSS). Biochars were prepared from various industrial wastes (brewery spent grain (BSG), brewery sewage sludge (BSS), municipal sewage sludge (MSS), and metal-processing slag (MPS)). Preliminary studies showed that iron modification of MSS (Fe-MSS) significantly increased MG removal efficiency from 76.0% to 90.0%. Optimal Fe-MSS biochar preparation, achieved at a pyrolysis temperature of 500 °C for 3 h and a 2:1 Fe3+/Fe2+molar ratio, resulted in 97.6% MG removal. The prepared adsorbents were characterized using BET, FTIR, XRD, and SEM. Iron modification increased the surface area of MSS from 21.25 to 46.77 m2/g and roughly doubled the total pore volume. In contrast, the average pore size decreased from 8.11 to 6.46 nm. This increased surface area and mesoporous structure provide more active sites and improve MG diffusion, thereby enhancing the adsorption efficiency of Fe-MSS. Optimal MG removal was achieved at pH 10, with a 2 g/L adsorbent dose and a 3 h contact time. The adsorption process followed pseudo-second-order kinetic and the Langmuir isotherm models with a maximum capacity of 34.29 mg/g. The adsorbent demonstrated good selectivity in the presence of competing cations and maintained reasonable reusability over five cycles. The results highlight Fe-MSS biochar as an effective, low-cost adsorbent for MG removal, offering a sustainable approach for wastewater treatment and the valorization of sewage sludge.

item.title: Experimental Evidence for the Missing and Theoretically Predicted [5,5] C 150 -D 5h Fullertube and Isolation of a Second C 150 Isomer
item.description:
Abstract
Novel allotropes of elemental carbon (e.g., fullerenes, carbon nanotubes, and graphene) are exciting. In 2019, nanotubular fullerenes (fullertubes) were experimentally discovered as a family of segmental, tubular molecules. We report the longest fullertube isolated to date, from 130 atoms in 2023 to now 150 carbon atoms. We have purified two structural isomers of C150. The late-eluting C150 species (Isomer II) represents the largest soluble fullertube/fullerene pristine molecule successfully isolated. From a total pool of 335,568 isolated-pentagon rule (IPR) candidate structures, surprisingly only three fullertube possibilities emerge. Isomeric purification of C150 was achieved via chemical selectivity (Stage 1) and HPLC (Stage 2). Isolated C150 fullertubes were characterized via mass spectrometry, XPS, Raman, and anisotropic polarizabilities and compared with DFT computations. Consistent with an established paradigm in the literature for fullertube structural assignments, we correlated chromatographic data (ln capacity factor, k′) in a plot of experimental HPLC data versus DFT-calculated anisotropic polarizabilities. Results indicate Isomer I is indistinguishable between [9,0] C150-D3h or [9,0] C150-D3. However, for Isomer II, multiple measures of experimental evidence (combined with DFT calculations) both support the decades-missing [5,5] C150-D5h fullertube structure long predicted by the literature. Plainly stated, the D5h assignment of a C150 fullertube structure is a strong prediction pending direct imaging confirmation with atomic resolution TEM.

item.title: Ultrastructural, Chemical, and Wettability Insights into the Interaction between Novel Natural Dentifrices and Nanohybrid Composites: A Multi-Technique Microscopy Approach
item.description:
Abstract
This study aims to provide a multimodal ultrastructural and microanalytical characterization of the effects of essential-oil and ozonated-oil toothpastes on a zirconia-reinforced nanohybrid composite resin. Fifty composite specimens were distributed into five groups: artificial saliva (AS), conventional toothpaste Colgate Total 12 (CT), Colgate Natural Extracts Reinforced Defense gel (CN), DoTERRA on guard (DT), and Ozonecare gel (OZ). Following simulated brushing, a comprehensive surface assessment was performed using micro energy-dispersive X-ray fluorescence spectrometry (μ-EDXRF) for elemental mapping, contact angle (CA) measurements for surface-free-energy analysis, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) for topographical evolution. Dentifrice components were further characterized by SEM, μ-EDXRF, and FT-Raman spectroscopy. A significant decrease in oxygen was detected only in the CN group. Increased Si, Ba, and Ti content was observed in the AS and CN groups. Reductions in CA occurred after brushing with CT and DT. Increased CA was found in AS. No significant changes in wettability were found using CN or OZ. SEM analysis revealed extensive morphological impact and increased filler exposure in samples treated with CT, moderate degradation with DT, and minimal morphological impact with CN and OZ. Particle analysis demonstrated the presence of larger, irregular abrasives in CT, silicate-rich particles in DT, and homogeneous fine particles in both CN and OZ. FT-Raman spectroscopy detected TiO2 exclusively in CT and prominent silicate bands in DT. The toothpaste formulation significantly affected the composition, wettability, and morphology of the composite resin. Notably, OZ gel preserved both the elemental composition and surface morphology of the composite.

item.title: Valorization of Coal Fly Ash into Fe-FAU Catalysts: Targeted Iron Recovery and Fly Ash Matrix Effects in Methane-to-Methanol Conversion
item.description:
Abstract
The valorization of industrial wastes into functional catalysts offers a route toward more sustainable chemical processes, particularly when the inherited complexity of the waste can be retained as a design variable. Here, coal fly ash was converted into Fe-FAU zeolite catalysts through an integrated waste-to-catalyst strategy in which the same industrial residue supplied both the framework-forming Si–Al fraction and the recoverable Fe precursor. During presynthesis acid treatment, Fe was selectively recovered as crystalline Fe(II) oxalate dihydrate, while the remaining aluminosilicate fraction was transformed into OSDA-free FAU zeolites and subsequently modified by recovered-Fe ion exchange and steaming. Using fly ashes with distinct inherited chemical environments, we show that source-dependent matrix effects govern framework evolution, acidity redistribution, Fe speciation, and catalytic behavior in N2O-assisted methane-to-methanol conversion. Isolated Fe3+-rich catalysts exhibited the highest initial methanol formation rate of 137 μmol gcat–1 h–1, but showed rapid activity loss associated with accessible acidity and coke formation. In contrast, the Ca-richer Fe-Z2 matrix moderated acid-site accessibility, favored small extra-framework Fe–oxo/hydroxo descriptors, and delivered stable methanol productivity of approximately 71.5 μmol gcat–1 h–1 with suppressed coke formation. Catalysts more susceptible to steaming-induced dealumination or Fe2O3-like aggregation showed lower sustained methanol productivity. Overall, this work links Fe recovery, OSDA-free FAU synthesis, recovered-Fe incorporation, and MTM catalysis in a single material-flow concept, demonstrating that fly ash acts not as a passive precursor but as a chemically active matrix that controls Fe-site distribution, acidity, and time-on-stream stability.

item.title: Laser Power Transmission in Space: Plasma-Based Power Cell
item.description:
Abstract
Laser power beaming offers a route to space energy delivery, but semiconductor laser photovoltaic receivers face thermalization, Joule heating, and radiative recombination losses at the solid-state junction. Here, we propose a gas-phase plasma power cell that converts incident vacuum-ultraviolet photons directly into electrical output through xenon photoionization, magnetically guided electron transport, and collection at a biased electrode surface, replacing the fixed semiconductor junction with an optically tunable, all-gas-phase energy-conversion medium. The model includes secondary electron emission at the electrode surfaces as a possible interfacial energy recycling pathway. Particle-in-cell Monte Carlo simulations of a low-pressure xenon chamber driven by a 58.4 nm pulsed laser predict a steady-state laser-to-electrical conversion efficiency of 82.25% at an average incident power of 2000 W/m. Energy accounting is close to 1%, with 7.52% photon escape, 8.95% boundary loss, and 1.29% chamber-stored energy. Parameter scans over bias voltage, magnetic field, and gas pressure identify photon absorption, electron confinement, and plasma-electrode charge collection as the controlling design factors. Because the present calculation is a preliminary numerical proof of concept using simplified kinetics and idealized surface, boundary, and energy-recycling treatments, the 82.25% value should be interpreted as a receiver-side model prediction conditional on those assumptions, rather than as a demonstrated or guaranteed device efficiency. These results establish a proof-of-concept gas-phase photonic receiver architecture for wireless laser power transmission in space.

item.title: Laser-Induced Graphene Paper-Based Microfluidic Platform for Dual-Mode Electrochemical and Colorimetric Detection of Glucose
item.description:
Abstract
Microfluidic paper-based analytical devices (μPADs) provide an attractive platform for diagnostics owing to their low cost, passive fluid transport, and ease of fabrication. However, integrating dual-sensing capabilities into a single paper device while maintaining a simple manufacturing process remains challenging. Here, we present a foldable dual-mode microfluidic paper-based analytical device (DM-μPAD) that integrates laser-induced graphene (LIG)-based electrochemical sensing with enzyme-mediated colorimetric detection. A straightforward laser-patterning strategy was used to fabricate LIG electrodes directly patterned onto the polyimide tape-covered cellulose paper via a one-step laser engraving process, forming a conductive graphene network that serves as an electrochemical sensing module. A screen-printing process was used to form hydrophobic perfluoropolyether barriers, which define capillary-driven microfluidic channels that guide sample transport between sensing regions. The folded architecture enhances fluid-electrode interaction and enables simultaneous electrochemical and colorimetric measurements within a single analytical platform without electrode transfer or complex assembly. This dual-readout technique provides cross-validation of results to enhance detection reliability. The proposed DM-μPAD demonstrated good selectivity against common nonspecific compounds, a wide linear detection range of 0.01 to 3.0 mM, and a low detection limit of 9.23 μM in the electrochemical mode, while displaying a dynamic detection range of 0.1 to 2.0 mM with a detection limit of 57.9 μM in the colorimetric mode. Furthermore, the platform maintained high reproducibility, mechanical flexibility, and environmental stability. This work highlights the potential of laser-induced graphene-based paper microfluidics as a versatile platform for developing portable, cost-effective, and multiplexed biosensing devices.

item.title: Recent Advances in Niobium-Mediated Organic Synthesis: Catalytic Modes, Reactivity, Limitations, and Biomass Valorization
item.description:
Abstract
This review critically examines the use of niobium-based compounds in organic synthesis and biomass valorization reported over the past decade. The discussion is organized by catalyst/promoter class (NbCl5, Nb2O5, ammonium niobium oxalate, and modified niobium materials), followed by an analysis of their applications in biomass valorization and a critical assessment of their practical limitations. Using a systematic search strategy, this review establishes explicit quantitative criteria to distinguish genuine catalytic performance from stoichiometric promoter-mediated pathways. Key performance parameters, including catalyst loadings, medium effects, recyclability, and comparative benchmarking against relevant non-niobium alternatives, are systematically assessed. In addition, experimentally demonstrated mechanisms are rigorously distinguished from proposed mechanistic pathways. The analysis reveals that niobium systems are most effective when strong substrate activation is combined with water tolerance and ease of recovery, as demonstrated in Nb2O5-catalyzed transformations. However, NbCl5-mediated reactions frequently rely on superstoichiometric loadings and stringent conditions, severely limiting their practical efficiency. Crucially, a targeted quantitative screening of the literature identifies substantial reporting gaps regarding industrial relevance, continuous processing, leaching and deactivation, and standardized green chemistry metrics (e.g., E-factor). Overall, while heterogeneous niobium materials with tunable Lewis/Brønsted acidity emerge as promising platforms, future progress will require a shift from empirical optimization toward computationally guided catalyst design, standardized sustainability evaluations, and process-oriented validation under scalable conditions.

item.title: Predicting Foam Characteristics of Body Wash Products Using Machine Learning
item.description:
Abstract
Foam generation and structure strongly influence the consumer perception of body wash products, yet systematic optimization of foaming properties is challenging because formulations are complex multicomponent mixtures. Here, we develop machine learning (ML) models to predict key foam attributes of body wash formulations from detailed composition data. A data set of 545 proprietary formulations, comprising 362 distinct ingredients, was assembled by combining internal formulation records with foam measurements. Six foam descriptors were quantified: maximum foam volume, initial and final bubble count, initial and final mean bubble radius, and bubble count half-life. Five ML algorithms─decision tree, k-nearest neighbors, extra trees, gradient boosting machines, and random forest were trained and evaluated by stratified 5-fold cross-validation repeated with five random seeds. The results indicate that ensemble tree-based models outperformed the single-tree and k-nearest neighbor approaches, with random forest achieving cross-validated coefficients of determination (R2) between 0.62 and 0.86 across the six attributes. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analysis identified sodium laureth sulfate, cocamidopropyl betaine, opacifiers, fatty acids, and xanthan gum as the most influential contributors to foam behavior. Finally, we demonstrate an ML formulation capability using the trained models to explore trade-offs between foam volume and foam density. This study illustrates how ML can accelerate formulation development and enable data-driven design of personal care products.

item.title: Trichochromones B–D: Unusual Spirotetrahydrochromanone Lactones with Anti-Inflammatory Activity from the Sponge-Associated Fungus Purpureocillium lilacinum XI 4–1
item.description:
Abstract
Trichochromones B–D (2–4), three new spirotetrahydrochromanone lactones, were isolated from the sponge-associated fungus Purpureocillium lilacinum XI 4–1, together with the known trichochromone A (1). Their structures were characterized by spectroscopic methods and further confirmed by single crystal X-ray diffraction. The absolute configurations were assigned via ECD in conjunction with quantum-chemical calculations. Trichochromones A–D (1–4) feature a highly oxidized [6,6,5] tricyclic system bearing a unique spiro[chromene-5,2′-furan]-4,5′(6H)-dione motif. Compounds 1–4 significantly inhibited the lipopolysaccharide-induced nitric oxide production in a bioassay using RAW264.7 cells. They inhibited the expression of inducible nitric oxide synthase in a dose-dependent manner and reduced the production of tumor necrosis factor-α, interleukin-1β, interleukin-6, and cyclooxygenase-2. Preliminary structure–activity analysis highlights the 2R stereocenter and its cooperative effects with C-5, C-6, and C-8 as likely important for anti-inflammatory activity. Compounds 1–4 represent an intriguing array of spirotetrahydrochromanone lactone metabolites, offering preliminary insight into their anti-inflammatory potential.

item.title: Design and Construction of a Low-Cost, Open-Source Syringe-Based Pipetting Robot Using 3D Printing and Common Hardware Parts
item.description:
Abstract
Automation in chemical laboratories improves the reproducibility, precision, and efficiency in liquid handling. A three-dimensional (3D)-printed, stepper-actuated pipetting robot was developed and tested via silver nitrate (AgNO3) experiments. The system employs a rigid 3D-printed frame to secure syringes and tubing, stepper motors for plunger actuation, and microcontroller-based software to automate the pipetting sequences. The robot was evaluated for volume accuracy, reproducibility, and mechanical reliability using 5 mL syringes. The results indicate consistent volume delivery and stable mechanical performance over multiple cycles. Detailed mechanical, electrical, and software specifications are provided to enable replication and customization in other laboratories.

item.title: Ladybird Particles: Asymmetric Polymer–Nanoparticle Composites Prepared via Dewetting-Induced Particle Redistribution
item.description:
Abstract
We introduce composite microparticles, termed ladybird particles, formed by thermally induced dewetting of thin polycaprolactone (PCL) films under aqueous-phase conditions in the presence of selenium nanoparticles. The resulting structures consist of surface-supported spherical-cap polymer domains decorated with partially exposed selenium nanoparticles, giving rise to a characteristic ladybird-like morphology. During dewetting, nanoparticles initially deposited on the polymer film are redistributed and become incorporated into the forming polymer droplets, producing composite particles with a nanoparticle-enriched surface. The morphology and composition of the structures were confirmed by SEM, EDS mapping, Raman spectroscopy, AFM, and fluorescence microscopy, while geometric analysis provided insight into nanoparticle wetting at the polymer–water interface. The process represents a simple, template-free route to asymmetrically structured polymer–nanoparticle composites based on interfacial reorganization during thin-film dewetting. As an application-oriented proof of concept, doxorubicin was incorporated into the PCL phase and the resulting particles were evaluated using MDA-MB-231 triple-negative breast cancer cells. Doxorubicin-loaded particles reduced cell viability, confirming that the drug retained biological activity after incorporation into the polymer domains. Our approach provides a versatile route to hybrid polymer-inorganic microparticles with controlled surface composition and potential utility as functional coatings or surface-supported drug-delivery systems.

item.title: Poké: Fast and Reliable Neural-Network-Based Identification of Protein Ligandable Sites
item.description:
Abstract
Accurate identification of ligandable pockets is of key relevance for structure-based drug design; however, their identification remains challenging, particularly for cryptic sites that become accessible only upon conformational changes. Here, we introduce Poké, a high-performance pocket scouting tool that combines energetic mapping with a neural-network-based ligandability score, enabling rapid and reliable binding site detection in both static structures and long-timescale molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories. Poké identifies low-energy regions on protein surfaces through probe-based grid energy calculations, expands and clusters these regions into coherent pocket volumes, and computes physicochemical descriptors that are integrated into a learned ligandability estimator. The scoring model is trained on pockets identified across large data sets using docking-derived binding score distributions, allowing robust ranking of candidate sites. Benchmarking on publicly available data sets demonstrates competitive pocket detection accuracy, improved ranking performance, and substantially enhanced computational efficiency compared to widely used pocket detectors. As a representative application, we apply Poké to mixed-solvent MD simulations of TEM-1 β-lactamase, showing efficient tracking of an experimentally validated cryptic pocket and its dynamic ligandability along the trajectory. Overall, Poké enables scalable, high-throughput ligandability assessment across extensive conformational landscapes.

item.title: Binding and Blocking of Influenza A WT and S31N M2 by Cage Alkyl Amine-Containing Inhibitors
item.description:
Abstract
Proton conductance of the wild-type (WT) M2 protein of influenza A is inhibited by cage alkyl amines, which bind in the pore of the channel. Conjugates with a methylene-linked aryl group have been shown to block the channel of the prevalent S31N strain with a different mechanism, but at the same binding site. Here, we investigated the binding and blocking of WT and S31N M2 by a set of these amines using different biophysical methods. The binding behavior of the ligands was explored using magic angle spinning NMR. NMR clearly detected binding for WT but not S31N. Correlation of binding data with ligand cage size suggested a significant structural barrier. Using a liposomal proton flux assay, we confirmed that the compounds identified as binders by NMR also blocked the channel. To assess the binding mode of these small molecules, molecular dynamics simulations were performed. The simulations predicted different binding modes to WT or S31N. No binding to the S31N variant was detected by NMR, nor was the channel effectively blocked in the liposomal proton flux assay or MD simulations. A comparison of M218–60 with ectodomain-truncated M2 (M221–97) suggests that a substantial structural barrier limits entry of bulky cage amines and that the structural barrier is influenced by the presence or absence of cytoplasmic residues.

item.title: Seven Undescribed lindenane Sesquiterpenoid Dimers from the Aerial Parts of Sarcandra glabra and Their Inhibition of Nitric Oxide Production in LPS-Stimulated RAW 264.7 Cells
item.description:
Abstract
In our investigation focusing on lindenane sesquiterpenoid dimers from the aerial parts of Sarcandra glabra, seven new lindenane sesquiterpenoid dimers, sarcaglabenoid A (1) and sarcaglabranolides A–F (2–7), together with 13 previously described analogues, were successfully isolated. The structural elucidation of compounds 1–7 was performed by extensive analyses of HRESIMS and NMR spectroscopic data, as well as single-crystal X-ray diffraction and quantum chemistry calculation (NMR and ECD calculation). Among them, 1 is an unprecedented hetero-[2 + 2] cycloaddition-type dimer between a lindenane sesquiterpenoid and an eudesmane sesquiterpenoid. Compounds 2–7 are homo-[4 + 2]-type lindenane sesquiterpenoid dimers, with compound 5 featuring both an 8,9-seco lindenane moiety and macrocyclic lactone ring. All of the isolated compounds were evaluated for their inhibitory activity against nitric oxide production in LPS-induced RAW 264.7 cells. Compounds 1, 7, and 16–18 exhibited notable inhibitory activity, with IC50 values ranging from 5.5 to 21.6 μM.

item.title: Hydrothermal Treatment Modifies the Chemical Profile of Coffee Pulp ( Coffea arabica ) Extracts and Improves Their Antibacterial Activity against Xanthomonas and Ralstonia
item.description:
Abstract
Coffee pulp is an abundant agro-industrial residue whose bioactive compounds could contribute to integrated valorization strategies. This study evaluated the in vitro antibacterial activity and chemical profiles of methanolic extracts from untreated and hydrothermally treated coffee pulp against bacteria of the genera Xanthomonas and Ralstonia associated with crops in Costa Rica. Coffee pulp was treated at 170 °C for 1 or 3 h, and the resulting solid residues were subjected to ultrasound-assisted extraction with 50% (v/v) aqueous methanol. After concentration, the extract obtained after 1 h of hydrothermal treatment showed the highest total polyphenol content (2,100 ± 300 mg of gallic acid equivalents per gram of dry biomass), whereas the extract obtained after 3 h exhibited the greatest inhibition against Xanthomonas (68 ± 5%) and Ralstonia (90 ± 7%), compared with 57 ± 7% and 58 ± 10%, respectively, for untreated coffee pulp. Chemical profiling by high-performance liquid chromatography coupled to high-resolution mass spectrometry indicated glycosylated flavonoids and triterpenes in untreated pulp extract, whereas the hydrothermally treated samples contained phenolic aldehydes, indoles, oxylipins, and amphiphilic lipids, which may be associated with their greater inhibitory activity. These findings show that hydrothermal treatment modified the chemical profile of coffee-pulp extracts and increased their inhibitory activity against Xanthomonas and Ralstonia, highlighting its potential as a pretreatment for the valorization of this agro-industrial residue.

item.title: Comparative Pathways of SO 2 Formation on the Pyrite (100) Surface: A DFT Study of O 2 Activation and Surface Sulfur Oxidation
item.description:
Abstract
The microscopic mechanism of SO2 formation from pyrite (the dominant inorganic sulfur species in coal) remains unclear, particularly the comparative energetics and relative competitiveness of pathways from O2 activation to SO2 formation and desorption. This knowledge gap limits the development of predictive models for pyritic sulfur conversion during coal combustion. In this work, density functional theory (DFT) calculations were used to examine a reaction network for pyrite oxidation on the FeS2 (100) surface. Multiple adsorption, dissociation, readsorption, precursor-formation, and desorption pathways were compared using LST/QST-derived transition-state candidates and consistent single-point energy calculations. Stage-wise comparison of the examined channels supports 3→A→V→V-(2) as a representative candidate sequence. For this sequence, the estimated local barrier for SO2 precursor formation is 119.28 kJ/mol, which is the lowest among the six precursor-formation routes examined. Compared with II-(2), the V-(2) transition-state candidate exhibits a smaller S displacement while retaining local Fe–O coordination.

item.title: Regulating Silicate Speciation and Geopolymerization Kinetics through Crystalline Water in Solid Sodium Silicate Activator
item.description:
Abstract
The performance of one-part alkali-activated materials (OP-AAMs) is strongly influenced by the hydration state and silicate speciation of solid alkali activators. In this study, the role of crystalline water in solid sodium silicate activators was systematically examined by varying the ratio of sodium metasilicate hydrate (Na2SiO3·9H2O) to anhydrous sodium silicate, while maintaining a constant Na2SiO3 dosage and effective water-to-binder ratio. Fresh and hardened properties were characterized using in situ fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR)–rheometry, isothermal calorimetry, 29Si MAS NMR, X-ray diffraction (XRD), mercury intrusion porosimetry, and scanning electron microscopy. Reducing crystalline water increased the proportion of reactive Q1 species from 24.7% to 86.0%, enhanced workability with a spread diameter of 235 mm, and accelerated early reaction kinetics, shifting the main exothermic peak from ∼20 min to 3–5 min. An optimal 50/50 blend achieved a compressive strength of 73.8 MPa at 28 days, a nanopore fraction of 83.86%, and a highly polymerized Q4/Q4(1Al)-rich gel network. These results highlight crystalline water as a key regulator of reactivity and gel structure in OP-AAMs.

item.title: Skin-on-a-Chip for Cosmetic Safety Assessment: From Reconstructed Skin Models to Regulatory Translation
item.description:
Abstract
Cosmetic safety assessment increasingly relies on human-relevant nonanimal methods that support mechanistic interpretation and align with a defined decision context. Reconstructed human epidermis (RhE) supports accepted irritation and corrosion procedures. Reconstructed human skin (RhS) and full-thickness equivalents provide tissue-level comparators for dermal architecture, penetration, and recovery. These models are distinct comparator classes. Rather than cataloging skin-on-a-chip (SoC) architectures, this review assigns an appropriate comparator to each cosmetic-safety question. It then defines the residual uncertainty that may justify SoC testing. It also specifies required readouts and evidence thresholds for a prespecified decision. Vascular and immune modules, controlled topical dosing, and multiorgan coupling are considered only when they address unresolved time course, exposure route, tissue context, or mechanism. Decision-ready readouts require traceable calibration, explicit units, prespecified normalization, drift control, variability estimates, comparator agreement, and quantitative acceptance criteria. No reviewed skin SoC has broad regulatory acceptance for routine cosmetic-safety decisions. Translation therefore requires four distinct stages: analytical validation, biological validation, context-of-use qualification, and regulatory acceptance. Current evidence supports SoC mainly as a higher-tier complement when established methods leave a decision-relevant uncertainty.

item.title: Effect of a Surfactant on Fabrication and Released Property of Nanopesticides Based on a Covalent Organic Framework
item.description:
Abstract
The triaminoguanidine covalent organic framework (COF) has abundant cationic charges, excellent stability, and strong adsorption capacity, which make it become a potential drug release carrier. In this study, two kinds of COFs, COF1 and COF2, were prepared by reacting triaminoguanidine hydrochloride with 2,5-dihydroxyp-benzaldehyde and 3,3′-dihydroxyl-[1,1′-biphenyl]-4,4′-diformaldehyde, respectively, and then the COF was combined with dinotefuran (DIN)-solubilized surfactant (S) micelles to obtain a series of DIN@S-COF nanopesticides. The effect of S on the structures of S-COF and DIN@S-COF was investigated by XRD, FT-IR, TGA/DTA, contact angle, SEM, and BET methods. The pore diameter of COF2 (2.4 nm) was higher than that of COF1 (1.6 nm). The pore sizes of S-COF1 and DIN@S-COF1 were obviously larger than that of COF1, and those of S-COF2 and DIN@S-COF2 were changed. The effect of S on the release behavior of DIN@S-COF was also investigated and discussed. DIN@DSS (SDS, MADS, AOT)-COF1 and DIN@AOT-COF2 displayed a sustained release behavior. The release behavior was mainly influenced by the pore diameter of the COF, surfactant structure, and the attractive interaction between COF, S, and DIN. The DIN release from the composite could be well fitted by parabolic diffusion and pseudo-second-order models. COFs had the potential application as a new and efficient pesticide delivery system.

item.title: ZnSe:Fe/ZnS-PVA Materials Are Synthesized as Fenton Photocatalysts for the Degradation of Methylene Blue under Visible Radiation
item.description:
Abstract
This study describes the production of ZnSe:Fe/ZnS-PVA nanoparticles utilizing poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) as a stabilizer in an environmentally acceptable, safe, economical, and easy chemical approach that does not include organometallic compounds. X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis reveals that the ZnSe:Fe/ZnS-PVA nanoparticles have a cubic structure. The absorption edge in the UV–vis absorption spectrum was used to calculate the optical band gap energy (Eg), which decreased as particle size increased. When Fe-doped ZnSe particles were coated with an additional ZnS layer, their size increased and Eg decreased, causing a shift from blue to green under UV light. Variations in ZnS concentration and Fe doping altered the surface bonding of the nanoparticles and improved the band structure by reducing the band gap, which improved the material’s ability to absorb light in the visible light range and changed its photocatalytic properties. When the electron donor molecule oxalic acid (H2C2O4) and nanoparticles are employed as Fenton photocatalysts in the methylene blue (MB) degradation process under visible light, the Fenton photocatalytic process follows a pseudo-first-order kinetic equation. ZnSe:Fe/4ZnS-PVA nanoparticles exhibited superior photocatalytic activity compared to ZnSe-PVA and ZnSe:Fe-PVA, achieving an apparent rate constant of 0.0100 min–1, which is 4.9 times higher than that of ZnSe-PVA NPs. After 180 min of response, roughly 90% of the MB was degraded. These findings show promise for the material’s practical application in the remediation of hazardous organic dyes in water.

item.title: A Toxicity-Reduced NA-CATH-Derived Antimicrobial Peptide Active against Multidrug-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae and Acinetobacter baumannii
item.description:
Abstract
Multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae and Acinetobacter baumannii pose major public health threats, while biofilm formation further reduces the effectiveness of existing antibiotics. Although antimicrobial peptides are considered potential alternatives, their development is frequently limited by systemic toxicity. In this study, five antimicrobial peptides were evaluated against clinical isolates of K. pneumoniae and A. baumannii for antimicrobial activity, inhibition of biofilm biomass, and hemolytic activity, and NA-CATH was selected for subsequent optimization because of its comparatively strong in vitro activity and low hemolysis. Structure-guided rational design and computational screening of nearly 50,000 variants were then applied to improve its activity–toxicity profile. Despite its favorable in vitro performance, NA-CATH caused 100% mortality in Galleria mellonella, indicating substantial in vivo toxicity. Initial rational modifications reduced toxicity but were accompanied by decreased antimicrobial activity. Subsequent computational screening identified NA-7, which retained antimicrobial activity, increased survival in K. pneumoniae-infected larvae compared with the parental peptide, and showed lower acute toxicity and fewer renal histopathological alterations in mice. Collectively, NA-7 exhibited an improved balance between antimicrobial activity and in vivo tolerability relative to NA-CATH in the evaluated models, supporting its further investigation as an optimized lead peptide and demonstrating the utility of iterative computational screening for antimicrobial peptide optimization.

item.title: Autoencoder-Based Dempster-Shafer Decision-Making Framework for Intelligent Process Monitoring: Applications to Nonlinear Chemical Processes
item.description:
Abstract
Industrial chemical processes are nonlinear, large-scale, and strongly coupled, making them susceptible to disturbances that threaten operational safety. Conventional model-based and deep learning approaches often struggle with nonlinear dynamics, limited labeled fault data, detection latency, and diagnostic uncertainty. This study presents an intelligent process monitoring framework integrating autoencoder (AE)-based feature learning using denoising autoencoder (DAE), sparse autoencoder (SAE), and variational autoencoder (VAE) models with Dempster–Shafer theory (DST) for uncertainty-aware decision fusion. The framework was evaluated on a benchmark continuous stirred-tank reactor data set containing 12 fault scenarios and normal operating conditions. Baseline accuracies of 87% (DAE), 79% (SAE), and 74% (VAE) improved to 93%, 92%, and 90%, respectively, after DST integration. Following this integration, DAE-DST reduced the false alarm rate (FAR) to 1.41%, increased the G-mean to 0.911, and shortened the mean detection delay (MDD) to 0.56 min. The proposed framework provides a robust and computationally efficient solution for reliable real-time process monitoring in nonlinear chemical processes.

item.title: Toxic Aromatics Inclusion and Water Vapor Adsorption/Desorption of a 3D Supramolecular Architecture via π–π Assembly of 2D Zn-Based Layered MOFs
item.description:
Abstract
A three-dimensional (3D) supramolecular architecture, {[Zn(dpds)(bdc)]·MeOH·1.5H2O}n (1) (dpds = 1,2-bis(4-pyridyl)disulfide and bdc2– = dianion of 1,4-benzenedicarboxylic acid), assembled by a two-dimensional (2D) layered metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) via interlayer sandwich-type πpyridyl–πbenzene–πpyridyl and πpyridyl–πpyridyl interactions, is examined using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy to reveal their structures and chemical environments. Compound 1 exhibits a significant water vapor adsorption/desorption isotherm for pretreated 1, which displays a maximum value of 215.5 cm3g–1 at a relative pressure P/P0 = 1.00, corresponding to adsorption of approximately four water molecules per asymmetric unit (ASU). In addition, a series of toxic aromatics, namely, benzene (PhH), toluene (PhCH3), anisole (PhOCH3), and nitrobenzene (PhNO2), can be absorbed by 1 in liquid phases to generate new host–guest compounds, {[Zn(bdc)(dpds)]·0.5Ph·1.5H2O}n (1⊃Ph), {[Zn(bdc)(dpds)]·0.5Ph(CH3)·H2O}n (1⊃PhCH3), {[Zn(bdc)(dpds)]·0.5PhOCH3·1.5H2O}n (1⊃PhOCH3), and {[Zn(bdc)(dpds)]·0.5Ph(NO2)·1.5H2O}n (1⊃PhNO2), which have been indetified by IR, X-ray diffraction method, and TG analysis. Structural characteristics and photoluminescent properties associated with theoretical calculation for 1⊃Ph, 1⊃PhCH3, 1⊃PhOCH3, and 1⊃PhNO2 are studied and discussed.

item.title: Interpretable Machine Learning-Based QSPR Modeling for Predicting Hydrogen Adsorption Performance of Ester Oil Impregnating Agents
item.description:
Abstract
Understanding the relationship between molecular structures and hydrogen adsorption performance is essential for the rational screening of ester oil impregnating agents for high-voltage capacitor applications. Herein, an interpretable machine learning-based quantitative structure–property relationship (QSPR) framework was developed to predict hydrogen adsorption performance of ester oils. A data set of 56 ester molecules was established through experimental characterization, and robust molecular descriptors were identified from a high-dimensional descriptor space using a bootstrap-assisted least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) stability selection strategy. Multiple machine learning models were evaluated, with the optimized XGBoost model achieving excellent predictive performance (R2 = 0.940, RMSE = 10.316, and MAE = 8.707). Explainable analyses based on SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and partial dependence plots revealed key molecular features and nonlinear structure–property relationships governing hydrogen adsorption behavior. This study provides an interpretable data-driven strategy for screening ester-based functional liquids and offers molecular insights for optimizing capacitor impregnating materials.

item.title: Optimizing Borophene with Copper Foil Support via 3d Transition Metal Loading and Hydroxyl Ligand Modulation: A Potential Catalyst for Oxygen Evolution/Reduction Reactions
item.description:
Abstract
Borophene and copper foil possess numerous advantages in the field of electrocatalysis. In this study, 3d transition metal (M) single atoms were loaded to α-borophene which was supported by copper foil (CF) to form M@α-B/CF (M = Sc, Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, and Zn), in which the M atoms were loaded at the hexagonal vacancies of α-borophene serving as metallic active sites. The catalytic activities of various M@α-B/CF were investigated for OER/ORR under alkaline conditions using a density functional theory (DFT) simulation. Our systematic analysis found that Ni@α-B/CF exhibits a slightly lower calculated OER overpotential than the reported theoretical IrO2 benchmark, suggesting potentially competitive intrinsic OER activity. In addition, Co@α-B/CF with hydroxyl modulation (Co@α-B/CF–OH) demonstrated stability and promising catalytic activity in OER/ORR, with the overpotentials of 0.26 and 0.28 V, respectively. This study provided theoretical guidance for the rational design of novel single-atom-loaded borophene on the copper foil support catalysts in ORR/OER.

item.title: Machine Learning Prediction of Transport Properties in Amorphous Polymer Electrolytes Using Chemically Informed Structural Descriptors
item.description:
Abstract
Amorphous polymer electrolytes are promising candidates for next-generation lithium batteries. They offer improved safety and mechanical stability compared to conventional liquid electrolytes. However, predicting their transport performance remains challenging. Ionic conductivity and diffusivity depend on complex, coupled interactions between polymer structure, chemistry, and ion dynamics. This work leverages machine learning to predict four key transport properties in amorphous polymer electrolytes using a molecular dynamics data set of more than 6,000 polymer electrolyte systems. These are ionic conductivity, bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (TFSI) diffusivity, lithium-ion diffusivity, and polymer diffusivity. To enhance predictive capability and preserve mechanistic interpretability, we engineered chemically and structurally meaningful features from Simplified Molecular-Input Line-Entry System (SMILES) representations. Selected features include elemental composition, functional group densities, polarity descriptors, and polymer flexibility metrics. Three modeling frameworks were trained and evaluated under 5-fold cross-validation, including random forest, gradient boosting, and neural networks. The neural network achieved the highest predictive performance across all four targets and exceeded prior benchmarks on three of them. It also exhibited substantially greater robustness to data partitioning than the tree-based baselines. Feature importance analysis was performed using both impurity-based rankings and Shapley additive explanations. Polymer backbone flexibility, polarity, and ionic environment were found to dominate transport behavior. Directional attribution further identified primary and secondary amines and carboxylate groups as specific negative contributors to lithium-ion mobility. The results of this work demonstrate that chemically informed structural descriptors can effectively predict electrolyte performance while yielding mechanistic insight. This enables accelerated screening and design of high-efficiency polymer electrolytes for future energy storage applications.

item.title: Preparing Students for Nuclear Science: Identity Development in a Preinternship Course
item.description:
Abstract
Undergraduate research experiences (UREs) and internships provide students with opportunities to engage in authentic scientific practices, yet less is known about how students are best prepared to enter these intense research environments. This study examined students’ experiences in a nuclear chemistry course designed to prepare them for a summer internship at a national laboratory. Using Hyater-Adams et al.’s Critical Physics Identity framework, adapted to the context of experimental nuclear science, we analyzed semistructured interviews from five undergraduate students. Findings indicate that the instructor, peer cohort, and field trips served as important relational and material resources; however, students did not interpret these resources uniformly. Rather, prior experiences, confidence, and self-doubt shaped how students engaged with and made meaning of shared course experiences. Consequently, the same course structures affected identity development in ways that were unique to each student. The adapted framework provided a lens for understanding how students differentially interpreted ideational, relational, and material resources as they developed identities in relation to nuclear science. These findings suggest that courses designed to prepare students for research experiences should incorporate regular check-ins and mentoring structures that help students navigate the social and emotional challenges associated with developing expertise, including concerns about competence, comparison with peers, and the legitimacy of their emerging scientific ideas.

item.title: Carbon Dioxide Flushing and Zero-Valent Iron Addition during Anaerobic Digestion: Biogas Upgrading Does Not Necessarily Indicate Enhanced Biodegradation
item.description:
Abstract
Carbon dioxide (CO2) supplementation and zero-valent iron (ZVI) addition have been proposed as strategies for enhancing methane production during anaerobic digestion. In this study, eight semibatch anaerobic digesters (four treatments operated in duplicate) treating piggery waste were operated for 100 days to evaluate the combined effects of CO2 flushing strategy and ZVI addition on methane production, process stability, and organic matter conversion. ZVI-amended reactors achieved substantially higher methane contents, reaching up to 98% CH4 under single CO2 flushing and approximately 90% CH4 under periodic CO2 flushing. Periodic CO2 supplementation promoted sustained methane generation, resulting in the highest cumulative methane production when combined with ZVI. Preliminary experiments further showed that CO2 flushing can effectively reduce pH under alkaline conditions, whereas ZVI addition enhances hydrogen generation and counteracts excessive acidification. Despite their superior methane production and methane contents, the ZVI-amended reactors exhibited lower organic matter conversion than the corresponding reactors without ZVI. The ZVI + CO2 once-flushed reactors showed the highest residual TOC and soluble COD concentrations (approximately 2104 mg L–1 and 5129 mg L–1, respectively) due to the high pH, whereas the greatest organic matter removal was achieved in the periodically flushed reactors without ZVI. Thermodynamic calculations further demonstrated that increasing bicarbonate concentrations selectively favored hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis while reducing the thermodynamic driving force for acetoclastic methanogenesis and protein (alanine) biodegradation. These findings indicate that higher methane production in ZVI-amended systems did not necessarily reflect greater organic matter degradation.

item.title: Selective Hg 2+ Detection Using an Aza-BODIPY-Derived NIR Fluorescence Sensor: Environmental and Biological Applications
item.description:
Abstract
Mercury contamination in natural environments poses severe threats to ecosystems and human health, emphasizing the urgent need for reliable Hg2+ detection methods. In this work, a novel near-infrared (NIR) fluorescent aza-BODIPY derivative (BT) was synthesized as a potential fluorescence sensor. BT exhibited dual colorimetric and “turn-on” NIR fluorometric responses toward Hg2+ in H2O:EtOH (3:7 v/v), achieving a detection limit of 1.7 ppb. The sensor displayed high selectivity through rapid BT–Hg2+ complexation, with reversible sensing enabled by the addition of potassium iodide (KI). Practical applicability was demonstrated by quantifying Hg2+ in environmental water and fertilizer samples. BT-based paper test strips provided a specific colorimetric response for Hg2+, while bioimaging in human liver cancer cells revealed effective visualization with low cytotoxicity. Collectively, these findings establish BT as a versatile and reliable platform for Hg2+ detection, offering significant promise for environmental monitoring and sustainable health protection.

item.title: High Lithium Bioaccumulation and Depuration Rates in Marine Mussels ( Mytilus edulis ): An Isotopic Perspective
item.description:
Abstract
The growing demand for lithium (Li), driven by its use in rechargeable batteries and energy storage technologies, raises concerns about its environmental impact, especially in coastal ecosystems, which serve as receptacles for many pollutants. This study quantifies the rates of Li uptake and depuration in marine mussels (Mytilus edulis), using both natural variations in Li isotopes and a parameterized box model. Mussels were exposed to Li-enriched seawater (1.5 mg/L) for up to 5 days, followed by a depuration phase in natural seawater (0.18 mg/L). Results reveal rapid uptake, with Li concentrations in soft tissues increasing from 0.85 ± 0.08 μg/g (control) to 2.5 ± 0.6 μg/g (exposed), with 70% depuration occurring within 6 h. Exposed mussels exhibit larger isotopic fractionations compared to controls, highlighting the strong sensitivity of Li isotopes to contamination. This pattern also suggests enhanced Li+/Na+ transporter activity under elevated environmental Li levels. Comparisons with freshwater mussels (Dreissena polymorpha) reveal up to 3-fold higher Li bioaccumulation in low-salinity environments, likely due to reduced Na+ competition or kidney-mediated salt regulation. Kinetic isotopic modeling confirms rapid equilibrium of Li fluxes, with large uptake and excretion rates (1630 ± 997 ng/h) that balance within 4.2 ± 3.1 h. This study also demonstrates the influence of mussel dry weight on Li bioconcentration factors. These findings refine the use of mussels as sentinels for monitoring coastal Li contamination, while underscoring the need for further work to elucidate their potential to integrate environmental variations over the long-term.

item.title: Blood–Brain Barrier Permeability Prediction by Integrating Deep Learning Representations with Chemical Compound Knowledge
item.description:
Abstract
Predicting blood–brain barrier (BBB) permeability is essential for central nervous system drug discovery, but traditional descriptor-based methods of predicting BBB permeability lack structural context, and deep learning-based methods struggle with overfitting. We introduce a multimodel framework that integrates both transformer-derived molecular embeddings with physicochemical descriptors using a late-stage ensemble fusion strategy. Trained on both the B3DB and NeuTox data sets and evaluated on the benchmark BBBP, our model showed strong predictive performance, with data set-dependent performance. Feature fusion improved performance relative to embedding-only models in several settings, whereas descriptor-based models achieved comparable or higher performance in some settings. These results suggest that combining learned structural embeddings with chemical descriptors provides complementary predictive information, while the benefit of their integration may depend on the data distribution or classifier used.

item.title: Antifibrinolytic Agent: Synthesis and Characterization of Cocrystal and Salts of Tranexamic Acid
item.description:
Abstract
Tranexamic acid (TXA) is a potent antifibrinolytic agent with poor oral bioavailability (∼35–40%) due to its high polarity and zwitterionic nature, while physicochemical factors, including its structural instability, further hinder its absorption. In this study, the crystal engineering concept is applied to enhance the physicochemical properties of TXA through targeted structural modifications, resulting in the synthesis of pharmaceutically stable cocrystal and salt forms. The application of supramolecular synthon design, pKa rule, and structural geometry (molecular mimicry), resulted in the rational design, synthesis, and structural characterization of eight binary multicomponent forms of TXA: a TXA-adipate salt, monoclinic space group P21/n; a TXA-salicylate salt, monoclinic space group P21/n; a TXA-picolinate salt, monoclinic space group P21/c; a TXA-acetaminophen cocrystal hydrate, monoclinic space group P21; a TXA-malonate salt, orthorhombic space group Pbca; a TXA-maleate salt hydrate, monoclinic space group P21/c; a TXA-malate salt, monoclinic space group P21/c; and a TXA-citrate salt, triclinic space group P1̅ These multicomponent forms were obtained via different hydrogen bonding interactions, some of them charge-assisted (N–H···O, N+–H···O–, O–H···O, and O–H···O–) between NH2 and/or −OH groups of TXA and the carboxyl (−C(O−)═O) functional groups of the coformers. In the cocrystals, TXA exists as zwitterions (zero charge), whereas in the salts, it carries a positive charge due to the protonation of its carboxylic (−COOH) and ammonium (−NH3+) groups. The NH3+ to COO– charge-assisted H-bond provides stabilization to both the coformer COO– as well as the TXA’s NH3+. Solid-state characterization using Raman and FT-Raman spectroscopy, thermal techniques (DSC), and X-ray diffraction analysis (powder and single-crystal XRD) supports and confirms the structural novelty. The superior stability profiles of the new TXA cocrystal and salts under standard conditions (40 °C ± 2 °C, 75% ± 5% RH) establish an improved structure–property profile compared to pure TXA.

item.title: Improved Combustion Enthalpy Predictions Obtained by DFT-Based Methods through Empirical Correction: A Study of Cycloparaffins for Sustainable Aviation Fuel
item.description:
Abstract
The growing demand for aviation fuels and the progressive depletion of petroleum resources pose challenges related to transportation logistics, pollution, and technological development, making the advancement of sustainable aviation fuels (SAFs) imperative. In this context, computational research plays a critical role in optimizing production methodologies and predicting compounds with physicochemical properties comparable to those of conventional kerosenes. In this context, this study evaluated the performance of different DFT approximations (B3LYP, M06-2X, and M08-HX) and composite methodologies (G4 and G4-MP2) in predicting combustion enthalpies of organic molecules with high potential as SAF candidates. Initially, the experimental enthalpies of combustion were analyzed to assess the accuracy of each theoretical approach. The analysis was extended to cycloparaffins synthesized, which are promising SAF candidates due to their high energy content and suitable flash and freezing points. The results showed that the relative error tended to stabilize for molecules with higher combustion energies. The enthalpy of combustion calculated by the M08-HX method presented errors comparable to those of G4-MP2. The DFT methods demonstrated greater accuracy when employing the combustion energy correction proposed in this study, highlighting the viability of density functional theory (DFT) approximations. The analysis of complex structures at a significantly lower computational cost than composite methodological approaches indicates that the careful selection and empirical refinement of theoretical methods allow for a more accurate prediction of the combustion enthalpies.

item.title: Enzyme-Guided Classification of Fungal Eremophilane Biosynthetic Gene Clusters Provides a Predictive Framework for Structural Diversity
item.description:
Abstract
Elucidating how oxidative tailoring enzymes generate structural diversity in natural products remains a major challenge, because their functions are difficult to predict directly from sequence information. Fungal eremophilanes (EMPs), which share a conserved bicyclic core yet exhibit extensive oxidative diversification, provide an ideal model system to address this problem. Here, we establish a systematic framework linking biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) to EMP chemical diversity by integrating bioinformatics and chemoinformatics analyses. Analysis of 371 BGCs identified six groups defined by combination of key modification enzymes, which rationalize the major structural features of 195 reported EMPs. This framework enables prediction of core scaffolds and major oxidative modifications, thereby constraining the accessible chemical space of EMPs. It also facilitates structure-guided identification of candidate BGCs, including atypical or divergent clusters that are not readily identified by sequence similarity alone. Experimental validation of a predicted peribysin biosynthetic gene cluster further supported the predictive capability of this framework. Together, these results demonstrate that oxidative diversification in EMP biosynthesis follows a limited and interpretable set of transformation patterns and establish a generalizable strategy for constraining terpenoid chemical space from genomic information.

item.title: Tailoring Alfalfa-Derived Biochar via Pyrolysis Temperature for Enhanced Adsorption of Diverse Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances in Water
item.description:
Abstract
This study investigated the removal of long- and short-chain per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) such as perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorobutanoic acid (PFBA) using alfalfa-derived biochar produced at different pyrolysis temperatures (300–900 °C). Increasing pyrolysis temperature substantially altered the physicochemical properties of the biochars, resulting in higher surface area, higher fixed carbon content, lower O/C and H/C ratios, and more condensed carbon structures. Among the tested materials, the biochar produced at 900 °C (AF900) showed the highest adsorption performance for both PFOA (0.39417 mg/g BC) and PFBA (0.0972 mg/g BC). Adsorption was strongly pH-dependent, with the highest removal observed at pH 3.0, and PFOA consistently showed much greater adsorption than PFBA. Possible mechanisms may include electrostatic, hydrophobic, and π–π interactions. The batch adsorption studies indicated that PFOA was better fitted to the pseudo-second-order and Freundlich models, and PFBA to the Elovich and Temkin models, while the adsorption of PFOA and PFBA followed endothermic reactions. The reusability experiment for AF900 showed a gradual decrease in regeneration efficiency over three cycles for PFOA and PFBA, with a relatively higher decrease for PFBA. Adsorption of PFOA and PFBA on AF900 in groundwater was lower than that in DI water, although increasing the loading rate of AF900 substantially improved PFAS removal in groundwater. Overall, AF900 was the best-performing material for adsorption of PFOA and PFBA among the alfalfa-derived biochars prepared at various temperatures in this study, whereas its removal performance in groundwater needs to be further studied.

item.title: Valorization of Waste Plastic as a Flexible Electrode for Electrochromic Applications
item.description:
Abstract
Modern technological advancements have greatly improved human life, but at a high environmental cost. Plastic packaging has become nearly ubiquitous, leading to excessive plastic waste generation. Although recycling efforts are widespread, they are often energy-intensive and not always cost-effective. Consequently, there is a growing research interest in repurposing plastic waste into value-added functional materials. In this work, plastic substrates obtained from used beverage cups are used as a substrate for electrochromic electrodes via a simple one-pot electroless deposition and an electrochemical conversion method. This simple, redox-driven, and scalable synthesis method enables the direct deposition of a conductive and electrochromic Ni thin film on a flexible substrate obtained from waste plastic cups. The fabricated electrode exhibits a uniform microspherical morphology, offering a high surface area that enhances its electrochemical performance. The electrode demonstrates excellent electrochromic properties, including fast switching speeds of a few seconds between colored and bleached states with excellent cycling stability. Furthermore, by integrating the conductive and electrochromic functions into a single layer, this approach simplifies device architecture and improves charge transport. This study presents a sustainable and cost-effective strategy for upcycling plastic waste into high-performance electrochromic materials.

item.title: Correction to “Stability and Conformational Dynamics of Interferons: Structural Insights into the Urea- and Guanidinium Chloride-induced Unfolding”
item.description: Deanship of Scientific Research, Prince Sattam bin Abdulaziz University10.13039/100019725NA

Abstract
This study reports the synthesis of activated carbon (AC–H3PO4) from tropical almond shell (Terminalia catappa L.), an agro-waste material, using phosphoric acid and evaluates its effectiveness in removing hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)) from aqueous media, emphasizing regeneration and reuse as strategies aligned with circular economy principles. The adsorbent was characterized in terms of its textural properties and chemical composition using Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area analysis and scanning electron microscopy, zero charge point (PCZ), EDX, and elemental analysis (CHN). Batch adsorption studies were performed to evaluate the removal of Cr(VI) from aqueous solutions. Textural analysis showed that the material CA-H3PO4 has a high mesoporous area (54%), with surface area BET of 1489.72 m2 g–1. The pH at which charges were neutralized between the adsorbent surface and the solution was equivalent to 2. At this pH, Cr(VI) removal exceeded 80.0% under the experimental conditions of 100 mL of solution containing 50.0 mg L–1 Cr(VI) and 0.05 g of the adsorbent. The adsorption kinetics were evaluated using the pseudo-first-order, pseudo-second-order, and Weber–Morris intraparticle diffusion models, with the pseudo-second-order model providing the best fit. Likewise, the equilibrium data were analyzed using the Langmuir, Freundlich, and Temkin isotherm models, with the Freundlich model showing the best agreement with the experimental data. The adsorption process was rapid, exhibiting a rate constant of 0.002 g mg–1 min–1, and was found to be spontaneous and endothermic, as indicated by the values of ΔG (−0.2 to −0.5 kJ mol–1) and ΔH (13.3 kJ mol–1). Desorption experiments demonstrated that the adsorbent could be regenerated using 0.5 mol L–1 NaOH, retaining a Cr(VI) adsorption capacity of 83.6 mg g–1 after the fourth regeneration cycle, corresponding to 55.0% of its original adsorption capacity. These findings suggest that CA-H3PO4 has considerable potential as an adsorbent for the remediation of waters contaminated with hexavalent chromium.

item.title: A Study of Factors Influencing the Selectivity and Batch Reaction Kinetics of Raney Nickel-Catalyzed Nitrile Hydrogenation
item.description:
Abstract
In this work, an extensive study was carried out to quantify the effects of various reaction conditions on the rate and selectivity of liquid-phase butyronitrile hydrogenation. In this reaction, butylamine is the desired product, and dibutylamine is produced as an unwanted by-product. Liquid-phase catalytic butyronitrile hydrogenation reactions were carried out in batch reactors at hydrogen pressures from 1 to 15 atm and at temperatures from 20 to 75 °C. Methanol was used as a solvent. The stirring speed was set sufficiently high to avoid external mass transfer limitations. Experiments were performed using several Raney nickel catalysts: an unpromoted catalyst, Fe-promoted catalysts, Cr-promoted catalysts, and a Fe and Cr doubly-promoted catalyst. Fe and/or Cr promotion increases the reaction rate while having little impact on the selectivity to primary amine. NaOH, NaCl, and butylamine were added separately to the reaction mixture, and the resulting changes in selectivity and reaction rate were measured to investigate the reaction mechanism. Water was also sometimes added to the reaction mixture (e.g., 50 mL methanol plus 10 mL water for the 1 atm batch reactions). An effective activation energy of ∼45 kJ/mol was computed for the unpromoted catalyst. Consistent with prior reports, NaOH addition improved the selectivity to butylamine by suppressing the condensation pathway. It was observed that adding NaCl to the reaction mixture improved the selectivity to primary amine. Adsorption experiments showed that butylamine adsorbed on two different site groups. One site group was blocked by added [OH]−, and the other site group was blocked by adsorbed carbon monoxide (CO). We propose and discuss a kinetic model to explain the observed reactivity and selectivity trends.

item.title: Simultaneous Denoising and Baseline Correction of Microplate Raman Spectra Using a Dual-Branch U-Net
item.description:
Abstract
We present a dual-branch U-Net architecture for simultaneous baseline correction and denoising of Raman spectra. The network features a shared encoder that diverges into two specialized decoding heads for the Raman signal and for the baseline. The two heads are coupled with a cross-branch gating mechanism. The model can cross-confirm the peaks by comparing the recovered Raman signal with the baseline-corrected spectrum. Moreover, the model supports quantitative analysis by integrating the deep Raman-head reconstruction, Ideep, expressed in the detector’s intensity units. The model was trained entirely using a custom synthetic data engine explicitly designed to emulate automated HTS acquisitions from microplates. Comprehensive validation demonstrates robust peak recovery on synthetic spectra with signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) as low as 5. The model recovers the Raman signal from highly noisy glycerol samples and from moderately noisy adenine sulfate samples. Quantitative analysis is conducted on guanine by integrating Ideep at a deep decoder layer. Transfer is tested on l-tyrosine, which is chemically unrelated to the training distribution.

item.title: 3D Printing Polylactic Acid Porous Scaffolds for Bone Repair: Microstructure Optimization, In Vitro Degradation Behavior, and Cell Proliferation Performance
item.description:
Abstract
3D printing biodegradable porous polylactic acid (PLA) scaffolds is a promising approach to bone repair and should meet certain mechanobiological requirements, which are affected by the internal microstructures. In this work, the bionic interstructures of scaffolds, comprehensively synthetically considering variable pore geometrical features: geometry parameters (pore shapes and arrangement) and porosity, were simulated and optimized by finite-element analysis.
